exclusions.name: Bank supervisor Elena Cruz
exclusions.why_safe: Elena Cruz oversees receipts but does not control collection rate or shipping schedule, so her actions do not affect the number of units received.

exclusions.name: Other hospitals or blood centres
exclusions.why_safe: The evidence only describes the Cascade regional blood centre and St. Vincent regional hospital. No other entities are mentioned as receiving or sending blood, so they are irrelevant.

uncertainties.meaning: The exact number of units collected each day is unknown because the drive operates at an average rate of 12 units per hour, but actual hourly yields may vary. Also, it is unclear whether the centre's stock after collection on Thursday (before the 4 PM shipment) is sufficient to fill the 150-unit cooler, or if there is a shortfall.

It is uncertain whether the centre will have at least 150 usable units by Thursday 4 PM to ship. The initial stock on Monday is 40 units, and collections occur Monday through Thursday (9 AM to 5 PM each day). The total collection hours from Monday 9 AM to Thursday 4 PM are 4 days × 8 hours = 32 hours, but the drive closes at 5 PM each day, so Thursday's collection before 4 PM is only 7 hours (9 AM to 4 PM). Total collection hours = 8 (Mon) + 8 (Tue) + 8 (Wed) + 7 (Thu) = 31 hours. At 12 units/hour, that yields 372 units. Adding initial 40 gives 412 units, which is well above 150. However, the Tuesday shipment of 150 units is sent at 4 PM Tuesday, so those units are removed from centre stock. After Tuesday shipment, centre stock = 40 + (Mon+Tue collection up to 4 PM Tue) - 150. Monday collection: 8 hours × 12 = 96 units. Tuesday collection before 4 PM: 7 hours × 12 = 84 units. So before Tuesday shipment, centre has 40 + 96 + 84 = 220 units. After shipping 150, centre has 70 units. Then Wednesday collection (8 hours × 12 = 96) brings it to 166 units. Thursday collection before 4 PM (7 hours × 12 = 84) brings it to 250 units. So centre has well over 150 units on Thursday. Thus this uncertainty is resolved: centre has enough.
The Tuesday shipment departs at 4 PM and takes about 3 hours, so it arrives around 7 PM Tuesday. The hospital receives it into its bank. This is known, so no uncertainty.
The Thursday shipment departs at 4 PM and takes about 3 hours, arriving around 7 PM Thursday. The deadline is Friday noon, so it arrives before the deadline. This is known.

The hospital's initial stock is 15 units. It receives the Tuesday shipment (150 units) on Tuesday evening, and the Thursday shipment (150 units) on Thursday evening. So by Friday noon, it holds 15 + 150 + 150 = 315 units. This is certain.
